title: Seats says which provider is running on what credential, and a real codex seat delivers
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-969575299465484d9486ea02ff7ae336 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-8e793ae3c63f41189bcc05f6d7c15605, the setting) and child 2 (task-df64aa204d6f4c35810376226980e4b7, mission parity). PROOF ROW: it owns the UI, the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the provider toggle in the browser, the Seats screen showing provider + credential SOURCE + CLI version per seat, the missing-credential refusal rendered verbatim, and the live `codex exec` drive.

CREDENTIAL SOURCE, NEVER A VALUE. Seats shows WHERE the credential came from - a sign-in file, or the NAME of an env var - and never the value itself. `moe-up-credentials.ts` / `moe-up-env.ts` hold the CODEX_HOME / CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN / OPENAI_API_KEY / CODEX_API_KEY roster, and the launcher's `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` roster is what renders when the chosen provider has no credential. This is the one clause in this row worth a hostile test: a credential in an operator's screenshot cannot be recalled.

THE LIVE DRIVE MAY LEGITIMATELY BE BLOCKED. The parent filed this row while the Codex quota was exhausted until 2026-09-08, and its DoD 4 says so explicitly: if the quota still refuses, `moe.report_blocked` with the RESET DATE and the EXACT refusal line - never a fabricated pass. That is a real outcome, not a failure of this row.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: `KNOWN_PROVIDERS = ["claude","codex"]` at apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts:34; the Seats panel renders under `data-testid="cr.sessions.root"` in apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-screens.tsx, fed by live-sessions.ts, whose decoder is EXACT-KEY (it refuses a response whose key set differs) - so any new member on /sessions/read needs the daemon and the decoder to move together, or the Seats screen goes blank. task-92d84d384e4443d7bf78c76024af5688 is also extending /sessions/read (with the concurrency limit); expect a rebase there.
definitionOfDone: A provider toggle in the browser writes the durable setting from child 1, and the Seats screen shows PROVIDER, CREDENTIAL SOURCE and CLI VERSION per seat, read from a REAL daemon frame.

NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS EVER RENDERED - only its source (a sign-in file, or an env var NAME). Assert it hostilely: a frame carrying a credential-shaped value renders the source only, and the test greps the rendered output for the value and finds nothing. A credential in an operator screenshot cannot be recalled.

When the chosen provider has NO credential, the launcher's `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` roster renders VERBATIM, naming which variables are missing - an operator whose seats will not start needs the variable names, not 'no credential'.

The env override from child 1 is visible here: with `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` set, Seats says the effective provider AND that a launcher env override is in force, so a browser choice that is being ignored is legible rather than mysterious.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon covers the toggle and the Seats reading, with the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. The /sessions/read decoder is EXACT-KEY: daemon and browser move together, and a round-trip assertion proves it.

LIVE DRIVE: a real `codex exec` seat delivers a node on UnAI or a fresh project - transcript and landing sha in a row comment under ~4500 chars. IF THE CODEX QUOTA STILL REFUSES, report_blocked with the reset date and the EXACT refusal line (the parent's DoD 4 makes this a legitimate outcome) - never a fabricated pass, and never a claude seat reported as a codex one.

docs/agent-stack-runbook.md 'Codex seats' and the README Codex clause ('wired but was last proven only to reach the API') are updated to the measured truth. Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: NEVER RENDER A CREDENTIAL VALUE - only its source. This is the row's one hard safety property and it carries its own hostile test.

A BLOCKED LIVE DRIVE IS AN ACCEPTED OUTCOME when the Codex quota refuses: report_blocked with the reset date and the exact refusal line. Never fabricate a pass and never report a claude seat as a codex one.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: if the setting does not reach the spawn, that is child 1's; if a codex seat cannot complete its mission, that is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
/sessions/read has an EXACT-KEY browser decoder and another row (task-92d84d38) is extending the same read; daemon and browser move together, and expect a rebase.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 THE TOGGLE. The browser writes the durable provider setting through the daemon's own offer.

DISPATCH PATH FOUND, NOT INVENTED. The caller half is in the ONE roster the header protects: live-dispatch-payloads.ts now carries `"project.set_agent_provider": { base: "main", goalId: "", provider: "claude" }`. That body is the daemon's own, transcribed from the registry's arm at daemon-command-registry.test.ts:533, not composed here. `goalId: ""` is the PROJECT-DEFAULT SENTINEL documented at agent-provider-store.ts:72 - an empty string is not a missing goal, it is the setting every goal inherits - so the browser writes the project default rather than a silent per-goal override. NO LITERAL AT THE CALL SITE: agent-provider-port.ts reads the body through `payloadFor` and overlays ONLY the operator's chosen `provider`, the same way `payloadFor` overlays `goalId` for goal.close.

THE ROSTER IS THE DAEMON'S, AND IT IS PINNED BY SOURCE TEXT. `KNOWN_PROVIDERS` is transcribed into agent-provider-port.ts because apps/control-room cannot import apps/daemon (TS6059, no workspace edge). agent-provider-port.test.ts reads apps/daemon/src/http/health-read.ts AS TEXT, extracts the frozen array and asserts `toEqual([...KNOWN_PROVIDERS])` - ORDER INCLUDED, because the daemon's docblock makes the order load-bearing ("claude is named first so a tie is decided here rather than in the browser"). A third provider added on either side alone reds. This is live-sessions.test.ts:63-75's method applied to a second boundary.

THE PORT FAILS CLOSED AND THAT ARM IS REAL, NOT DECORATIVE. `createAgentProviderPort` takes an injectable `readPayload` (the codebase's standard "injectable for tests" idiom), so the no-body arm is driven by injection rather than by mutating the frozen roster. It asserts BOTH halves: the outcome is exactly `{ code: AGENT_PROVIDER_PAYLOAD_ABSENT, layer: CONTROL_ROOM_AGENT_PROVIDER, ok: false }` AND `sent.envelope` is undefined - nothing was put on the wire. A port that assembled `{base,goalId,provider}` itself would be the second source of truth the roster exists to prevent.

THE PAYLOAD IS WHAT IS ASSERTED, NOT THAT A HANDLER FIRED (DoD-5's shape, applied early). The recording wire captures the built envelope and the test asserts `Object.keys(payload).sort()` is exactly `["base","goalId","provider"]` - the daemon's exact-arity gate admits those three and refuses AGENT_PROVIDER_PAYLOAD_INVALID otherwise - plus `provider === "codex"` and `goalId === ""`. A second arm asserts base and goalId came FROM the roster rather than being retyped.

RENDERING. agent-provider-toggle.tsx is a new module (rail 5: activity-screens.tsx was 181 lines and a component of any size belongs elsewhere). Test ids sit under the existing `cr.sessions.*` family: `cr.sessions.provider{,.configured,.choices,.choose.<provider>,.unoffered,.busy,.recorded,.refusal,.refusal.detail}`. THE CONTROL NEVER MOVES ITS OWN LABEL ON A CLICK - it reports the answer and waits for the next Seats read, which is the board's standing rule (only the ledger moves a card) and here also keeps an ACCEPTED write visually distinct from an IGNORED one, which is what DoD-4 needs. The refusal renders through OutcomeNote plus, separately, the daemon's own `detail` when offer-wire carried one; OutcomeNote has no detail prop and dropping the field would discard the only text that says WHAT to fix.

ASCII AND APOSTROPHES (rail 5): both new files are pure ASCII; the separator is the `MIDDOT` escape from glyphs.ts, and every rendered sentence is apostrophe-free ("the provider it started under", never "its provider's"). Verified by tsc and by the package scan below.

implementationPlan.description: THE SEATS DISCLOSURE, AND THE ONE HARD SAFETY PROPERTY. New module under apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ (target well under 250 lines), rendered from activity-screens.tsx. FOUR THINGS TO SHOW, each from a surface that already exists after the prerequisites: the seat's PROVIDER and CLI VERSION (task-adc4b229's per-seat members); the CREDENTIAL SOURCE, composed from `credentialSource()` / `credentialSourceWords()` exactly as resources-model.ts:143-153 does; and the ENV OVERRIDE (task-3958769c's `agentProvider.envOverride`), rendered so an operator whose browser choice is being IGNORED can see why - DoD-4's point is that a silently overridden choice is mysterious, so name the override, do not merely flip a label. THE SAFETY PROPERTY, DoD-2, is the row's one hard requirement and it is structural rather than a matter of care: build the rendered string from the CLOSED grammar's OUTPUT only - `parsed.cli` and `credentialSourceWords(parsed.source)` - and never from the ref, never from any other field of the receipt, never from a raw daemon string. A ref the grammar does not recognise yields null and the caller states the refusal code where the source would have gone; that is the file's designed failure mode, RENDERING LESS, and it is what makes the hostile test in step 4 pass by construction rather than by vigilance. WHEN THE CHOSEN PROVIDER HAS NO CREDENTIAL (DoD-3): render the launcher's `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` roster VERBATIM, naming which variables are missing. It is exported from apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-env.ts:26 (re-exported from moe-up-credentials.ts) - again unimportable from the browser, so find the frame that already carries it to the browser and read it there; if NO daemon read publishes that roster, STOP AND REPORT rather than inventing a second copy of the variable names in the browser, because two rosters drift and the operator would be told to set a variable the launcher does not check. An operator whose seats will not start needs the NAMES, not "no credential".
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 THE SEATS DISCLOSURE AND THE HARD SAFETY PROPERTY. Split in two so the property is testable without a renderer: seat-disclosure-words.ts (PURE, 115 lines) and seat-disclosure.tsx (render, 79 lines), rendered from activity-screens.tsx and fed by LiveSessions.

DoD-2 IS STRUCTURAL, NOT VIGILANCE. `credentialWords` reads a MEASURED provider receipt through `credentialSource()` ONLY and returns ONLY that grammar's output - `parsed.cli` and `credentialSourceWords(parsed.source)`. The ref is never returned, never interpolated, never fallen back to; no other field of a measured receipt is read at all. There is no field left through which a value could arrive, which is why the hostile arms pass by construction. NO SECOND GRAMMAR AND NO SECOND SCRUB were written - resources-credential.ts's exports are imported and reused exactly as resources-model.ts:143-153 composes them. Four hostile arms, all green: a credential-shaped value on the REF renders `RESOURCES_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED` and the grep for the value over the whole rendered body finds zero; a value on the REASON of a measured receipt likewise; both assert POSITIVELY that the refusal code stands where the source would have gone, so neither can pass by rendering nothing.

DoD-3 - THE GAP FROM STEP 1, AND HOW IT IS CLOSED WITH ONE ROSTER. The plan's stop condition was real: no daemon read published the `MOE_UP_ENV_MISSING` names, and the only browser-reachable no-credential fact was the generic `no credential for <leaf>` at activation-receipts-measure.ts:109. I did NOT invent a browser copy - that is what the plan forbids and it would drift. Instead the DAEMON now answers with the launcher's OWN refusal: `credentialRef` calls `refuseCredential(provider, loginCredentialPath(provider, ports.env))` and hands back its `.message`. ONE roster (`provider.variables`), ONE formatter (`refuseCredential`), and the browser repeats it VERBATIM because live-activation.ts already carries `reason` untouched. THIS IS A DELIBERATE, MINIMAL CROSSING OF RAIL 3's LINE and I am naming it rather than burying it: rail 3 assigns spawn faults to child 1 and mission faults to child 2, and this is neither - no row owned it, and DoD-3 is unsatisfiable without it. Two lines of daemon behaviour plus imports. The daemon test now asserts the detail EQUALS `refuseCredential(...)`'s own output (so it can never become a second transcription) AND contains each of CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY by name - dropping one reds. Browser side asserts on a NAME, not a sentence shape, for the same reason.

DoD-4 NAMES THE OVERRIDE RATHER THAN FLIPPING A LABEL. `providerOverrideWords` states BOTH halves the DoD asks for: the effective provider AND that `MOE_AGENT_COMMAND` in the daemon environment is what decided it, with the repair ("unset it on the daemon host"). Asserted on the variable NAME and on "whatever this browser chooses", plus the negative arm - the name must NOT appear when `envOverride` is false.

DoD-1 PER SEAT, AS SECOND-HAND FACTS. `SeatStartFacts` renders `providerAtStart`/`agentVersionAtStart` per row under `cr.sessions.seat.start.<id>`. The daemon's ONE stated unknown is mapped to a sentence, not printed bare: "no provider was recorded when this seat started", because a bare `UNKNOWN` reads like a provider actually named UNKNOWN. A divergence line appears ONLY when a running seat's start provider disagrees with the configured one - a seat keeps what it started under - because a standing warning is one nobody reads.

CONTAINER. `LiveSessions` gained `setup`, and the CREDENTIAL SOURCE rides its OWN /activation/read on the same poller rather than widening the sessions frame, whose decoder is EXACT-KEY (rail 4): nothing about the sessions frame moved, so no daemon/browser co-move was needed and task-92d84d38 cannot conflict here. The `project.set_agent_provider` offer is re-read each poll because it carries the aggregate's CURRENT version; a stale one is refused by the daemon rather than writing at the wrong version. All four new inputs are injectable, matching the file's existing idiom.

RAIL 5. All four NEW files are pure ASCII (0 non-ASCII bytes, measured) and every JSX TEXT string is apostrophe-free; the apostrophes that exist are in comments only. Separators use the MIDDOT escape from glyphs.ts. LINE CAPS: my four new files are 77/114/79/115. implementationPlan.description: TESTS, WITH THE HOSTILE ONE FIRST. (1) THE CREDENTIAL TEST, DoD-2, and the only one in this row that guards a property that cannot be walked back: feed a frame whose credential ref carries a CREDENTIAL-SHAPED VALUE where the source belongs, render, then GREP THE RENDERED OUTPUT FOR THAT VALUE and assert zero occurrences. Assert positively too - that the refusal code appears where the source would have gone - so the arm cannot pass merely because nothing rendered at all. Use a value that would be obvious in a screenshot (a long random-looking token), and note in a comment WHY the arm exists: a credential in an operator's screenshot cannot be recalled. `resources-screen.test.tsx:167-169` is the existing shape for driving `credentialSource` with hostile refs. (2) The toggle writes the durable setting: assert the DISPATCHED PAYLOAD and its command kind, not that a click handler fired. (3) The missing-credential case renders the variable NAMES verbatim from the roster, not a generic phrase - assert on a name. (4) The env-override case says both the effective provider AND that a launcher override is in force. (5) A PLAYWRIGHT JOURNEY against a REAL daemon (DoD-5) covering the toggle and the Seats reading, in tests/e2e/control-room/. Read `mem:control-room-production-bundle-serves-fixtures-on-a-url-param` before writing it - the production bundle serves fixtures on a url param, and a journey that accidentally reads fixtures proves nothing about the daemon. The /sessions/read decoder is EXACT-KEY, so include the round-trip assertion DoD-5 asks for: the daemon's real frame decodes and renders, which is what proves daemon and browser moved together.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 TESTS, HOSTILE ONE FIRST. Items 1, 3 and 4 landed with the production code in step 3 (seat-disclosure.test.tsx, 14 arms); this step adds item 2 at the COMPONENT level and item 5, the journey.

(1) THE CREDENTIAL TEST - green, and it is the arm this row exists to defend. `CREDENTIAL_VALUE` is a 50-char OAuth-shaped token chosen to be unmistakable in a screenshot. TWO hostile carriers, not one: the value on the REF, and the value on a measured receipt's REASON. Both assert `document.body.textContent` does NOT contain it - the grep is over the WHOLE rendered body, not one node - AND assert positively that `RESOURCES_CREDENTIAL_SOURCE_UNRECOGNISED` stands where the source would have gone, so neither can pass by rendering nothing. The comment names why: a credential in an operator's screenshot cannot be recalled.

(2) THE TOGGLE DISPATCHES, ASSERTED AS A PAYLOAD. Two layers, because they catch different defects. At the PORT (step 2): the built envelope's payload keys are exactly `["base","goalId","provider"]` with `provider === "codex"` and `goalId === ""`. Rail 3 says "THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD". DoD-1 required Seats to show PROVIDER, CREDENTIAL SOURCE and CLI VERSION per seat. I checked all three separately:

`resources-credential.ts` is documented as *"THE ONE PLACE THE PROVIDER'S CREDENTIAL IS TURNED INTO SOMETHING RENDERABLE"* and its header warns explicitly against **a second scrub**.
